questions.q: **Win + Left arrow** does what to the current window?
options: Snaps it to the left half of the screen
Moves it to another monitor only
questions.solution: **Snap**: Win+Left/Right parks the window on that half; Win+Up maximises; Win+Down restores or minimises.

questions.q: Which of the following is **NOT a valid** file name in Windows?
questions.solution: The colon (**:**) is one of the forbidden characters (\ / : * ? " < > |) because Windows reserves it for drive letters. The other names are legal.
questions.shortcut: Drive letters use the colon, so file names cannot.

questions.q: Which shortcut opens an **Incognito (private) window** in Chrome/Edge?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+N** — Chrome and Edge. Firefox uses Ctrl+Shift+P.

questions.q: Which of the following is **application** software?
questions.solution: **MS PowerPoint** produces the user's slides — an application. Windows 11 is an OS, a driver is system software, and the Defragmenter is a utility.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: **Apply to** an organisation, **apply for** a post. The blank is followed by 'three banks' — organisations — so: **to**. ('He has applied for the clerical post' would use *for*, because a post is the thing requested.)
questions.shortcut: Organisation after the blank → apply to; post → apply for.
questions.passage: Suresh delivers parcels by day and studies for the bank examination by night. He is not ashamed (1) ______ his timetable: thirty minutes of maths on the bus, an hour of English after dinner. His wife manages the accounts of a small jeweller, and the couple rarely watch television (2) ______ Sundays. Suresh has applied (3) ______ three banks so far and keeps a diary of every exam date. His friends laugh at the diary, but he says a man who cannot put (4) ______ small pleasures for a year does not deserve a big one.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Permissible**: the stem 'permiss' is not a complete word, and the related noun is permission, so the ending is **-ible**. The s is doubled, as in permission.

questions.q: What does Harish mean when he says, 'Now it means extra money'?
options: He has started a business selling solar panels
Sunny days make his crops fetch higher prices
The power company pays him more than he earns from farming
Surplus solar power is now sold instead of being spent on extra pumping
questions.solution: The contrast is with 'Earlier, extra sunshine meant extra pumping'. Now the extra power is sold to the power company under the scheme. He sells electricity, not panels; crop prices are not discussed; and he calls the payment 'small but steady', so 'more than farming' is unsupported.
questions.shortcut: Read the quoted line together with the line it contrasts with ('Earlier…').
questions.passage:
When Harish replaced his diesel pump with a solar one, his monthly fuel bill fell to zero. For the first time, he could water his fields in the afternoon without worrying about cost, and he did — often for longer than the crop needed. Two years later, the water in his borewell had dropped by several metres.

His neighbours noticed. Some of them have now joined a scheme under which farmers can sell spare solar electricity to the power company instead of using it to pump more water. Harish says the payment is small but steady. 'Earlier, extra sunshine meant extra pumping,' he says. 'Now it means extra money.'

questions.q:
Select the correct question tag.

Nobody called while I was out, ___
questions.solution: *Nobody* makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive; indefinite pronouns for people (*nobody, everyone, someone*) are picked up by **they**. The simple past *called* takes *did* → **did they?**
questions.shortcut: Negative word → positive tag; nobody → they.

questions.q: The five sultanates born from the Bahmani breakup include **Berar**, ruled by the —
questions.solution: Five heirs: **Bijapur (Adil Shahi), Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahi), Golconda (Qutb Shahi), Berar (Imad Shahi), Bidar (Barid Shahi)**.

questions.q: Pairing **award ↔ field, day ↔ theme, index ↔ publisher** belongs to which frame?
questions.solution: Match-the-column tests **pairs** — the safest method is checking each pair independently; one verified wrong pair eliminates the whole option.

questions.q: **Tansen**, one of the Navaratnas, adorned the court of —
questions.solution: **Tansen** — Akbar's court musician, the fountainhead of Hindustani music and the Miyan ki Malhar raga lore.

questions.q: Which Mauryan officer kept charge of the **treasury and storehouses**?
questions.solution: The **Sannidhata** was treasurer–storekeeper; the **Samaharta** collected revenue; **Rajukas** measured land; **Gramika** headed the village.

questions.q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 4 and 120 respectively. How many different pairs of such numbers are possible?
The minimum value of $4\tan^2\theta+9\cot^2\theta$ (for acute $\theta$) is:
questions.solution:
By AM–GM, $4\tan^2\theta+9\cot^2\theta\ge2\sqrt{4\times9}=12$,

with equality when $2\tan\theta=3\cot\theta$, i.e. $\tan^2\theta=\frac32$ (reachable since tan is unbounded).

questions.q: A cable of length $60$ m runs from the top of a pole to the ground, making $60^\circ$ with the ground. The height of the pole is:
questions.solution: $h = 60\sin60^\circ = 60 \times \frac{\sqrt3}{2} = 30\sqrt3$ m.
questions.shortcut: Hypotenuse × sin60. Trap: $60\sqrt3$ — forgetting to halve.

questions.q: Find the HCF of 96, 240 and 384.
**P is 11th from the left end and Q is 9th from the right end of a row of 30 people. How many people are between them?**
questions.solution: Opposite ends: $30 - 11 - 9$ = **10** between.

questions.q:
Study the pattern and find the missing number.

**Grid 1:** 3, 5, 16  **Grid 2:** 4, 6, 25  **Grid 3:** 5, 7, ?

(Each grid is read left to right as one row.)
questions.solution: Grid 1: 3 × 5 + 1 = 16; grid 2 confirms: 4 × 6 + 1 = 25 ✓. Grid 3: 5 × 7 + 1 = **36**. (35 is the bare product.)
questions.shortcut: Solve grid 1, confirm on grid 2, apply to grid 3.

questions.q:
**Statement:** A train covered a distance of 360 km in 4 hours 30 minutes.

**Conclusions:**
I. The average speed of the train was 80 km/h.
II. The speed of the train never exceeded 80 km/h.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: I: 360 ÷ 4.5 = 80 km/h — **follows**. II: an average says nothing about the maximum; the train could have run faster on some stretches and slower on others — **does not follow**. Answer: **Only I**.
questions.shortcut: Average speed fixes the average, never the top speed.

questions.q: Six people — A, B, C, D, E and F — sit in a row facing north. **D sits at the left end. B sits fourth to the right of D. E sits to the immediate left of B. A is not a neighbour of D. C sits at one of the ends.** Which of the following is **true**?
options: C sits third to the right of E
F sits to the immediate right of D
E sits at one of the ends
questions.solution: D = 1, B = 5, E = 4, C = 6 (the only free end). Seats 2 and 3 remain; A is not next to D, so A = 3 and F = 2. Row: D F A E B C. F is immediately right of D — true. E is at seat 4 (not an end), A and B have E between them, and C is second (not third) to the right of E.
questions.shortcut: Solve the row completely once; then each option is a 5-second check.
